title: Which one's better?
goal: Compare two phones with Sēf: better, cheaper, more expensive, lighter, faster
tip: To compare, use the afʿal shape + min 'than': rkhīṣ → arkhaṣ 'cheaper', ghāli → aghla 'more expensive', zēn → azyan or aḥsan 'better'. It never changes for gender: hādha aḥsan, hādhi aḥsan. Say 'by how much' with b-: aghla b-miya 'a hundred more'.
grammar: Comparative afʿal + min: aḥsan min 'better than'; the same form for masculine and feminine
dialogue: B
سيف، أي واحد أحسن؟ هذا ولّا هذاك؟
Sēf, ay wāḥid aḥsan? hādha walla hādhāk?
Sēf, which one's better? This one or that one?
سَيْفْ، أَيْ وَاحِدْ أَحْسَنْ؟ هٰذَا وَلَّا هٰذَاكْ؟
A
هذا أحسن من هذاك، بس أغلى. تبيه؟
hādha aḥsan min hādhāk, bas aghla. tabīh?
This one's better than that one, but it's more expensive. Do you want it?
هٰذَا أَحْسَنْ مِنْ هٰذَاكْ، بَسْ أَغْلَى. تَبِيهْ؟
B
أغلى بكم؟
aghla b-cham?
How much more?
أَغْلَى بْكَمْ؟
A
بمية بس. والكاميرا حقه أزين
b-miya bas. w il-kāmīra ḥaggah azyan
Only a hundred. And its camera is better.
بْمِيَة بَسْ. وْالْكَامِيرَا حَقَّهْ أَزْيَنْ
B
بس هذاك أخف وأصغر
bas hādhāk akhaff w aṣghar
But that one's lighter and smaller.
بَسْ هٰذَاكْ أَخَفّْ وْأَصْغَرْ
A
صح، بس هذا أسرع. المهم، شو تبي، أرخص ولّا أسرع؟
ṣaḥḥ, bas hādha asraʿ. il-muhimm, shu tabi, arkhaṣ walla asraʿ?
True, but this one's faster. Anyway, what do you want, cheaper or faster?
صَحّْ، بَسْ هٰذَا أَسْرَعْ. الْمُهِمّْ، شُو تَبِي، أَرْخَصْ وَلَّا أَسْرَعْ؟
B
أسرع. خلاص، أبيه، يستاهل
asraʿ. khalāṣ, abīh, yistāhil
Faster. OK, I'll have it, it's worth it.
أَسْرَعْ. خَلَاصْ، أَبِيهْ، يِسْتَاهِلْ
items: never changes: hādhi aḥsan (this one (f.) is better); aḥsan min = better than
from ghāli; aghla b-miya = a hundred more
from zēn; aḥsan is more common
for a feminine thing: ay waḥda?
it's worth it; he deserves it
ma yistāhil = it's not worth it

title: A bigger size?
goal: Try on a shirt with Sēf: too tight, too loose, another size or colour
tip: Sizes compare like prices: akbar 'bigger', aṣghar 'smaller'; add shwayy for 'a bit': aṣghar shwayy. Colours have the same shape (aḥmar 'red', azrag 'blue') but they aren't comparatives: they change for a feminine noun (ḥamra, zarga), while akbar and aḥla never change.
grammar: Comparatives of size (akbar, aṣghar shwayy); colour words look like comparatives but agree (shown in the notes)
dialogue: B
سيف، هالقميص ضيق علي
Sēf, hal-gamīṣ ẓayyig ʿalay
Sēf, this shirt's tight on me.
سَيْفْ، هَالْقَمِيصْ ضَيِّقْ عَلَيْ
A
جرب مقاس أكبر
jarrib magās akbar
Try a bigger size.
جَرِّبْ مَقَاسْ أَكْبَرْ
B
هذا أكبر، بس واسع شوي
hādha akbar, bas wāsiʿ shwayy
This one's bigger, but it's a bit loose.
هٰذَا أَكْبَرْ، بَسْ وَاسِعْ شْوَيّْ
A
جرب الأزرق، هو أصغر شوي
jarrib il-azrag, huwa aṣghar shwayy
Try the blue one, it's a bit smaller.
جَرِّبْ الْأَزْرَقْ، هُوَ أَصْغَرْ شْوَيّْ
B
الأزرق؟ لا، ما أبيه. عندهم أحمر؟
il-azrag? la, ma abīh. ʿind-hum aḥmar?
The blue one? No, I don't want it. Do they have red?
الْأَزْرَقْ؟ لَا، مَا أَبِيهْ. عِنْدْهُمْ أَحْمَرْ؟
A
هيه، بس والله الأزرق لايق عليك، أحلى من الأحمر
hē, bas wallāh il-azrag lāyig ʿalēk, aḥla min il-aḥmar
Yes, but honestly the blue would suit you, it's nicer than the red.
هَيْه، بَسْ وَاللّٰهْ الْأَزْرَقْ لَايِقْ عَلَيْكْ، أَحْلَى مِنْ الْأَحْمَرْ
B
خلاص، عطني إياه
khalāṣ, ʿaṭni iyyāh
OK, give it to me.
خَلَاصْ، عَطْنِي إِيَّاهْ
items: from kbīr; akbar minni = older than me
you'll also hear sāyz (سايز), from English
to a woman: lāyig ʿalēch (لايق عليج)

title: The best one in the shop
goal: Buy a perfume for your mum in the souq: ask for the best, react to the price, bargain
tip: afʿal before a noun means 'the most': aḥsan wāḥid 'the best one', aghla wāḥid 'the most expensive one', aḥsan shay 'the best thing'. No il- is needed: hādha aḥsan wāḥid ʿindi 'this is the best one I've got'.
grammar: Superlative: afʿal + wāḥid / shay / noun (aḥsan wāḥid, aghla wāḥid, aḥsan shay)
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. أبي عطر حق أمي. شو أحسن شي عندك؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. abi ʿiṭir ḥagg ummi. shu aḥsan shay ʿindak?
Hello. I want a perfume for my mum. What's the best thing you have?
السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَبِي عِطِرْ حَقّْ أُمِّي. شُو أَحْسَنْ شَيْ عِنْدَكْ؟
A
وعليكم السلام. هذا أحسن واحد عندي، دهن عود
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. hādha aḥsan wāḥid ʿindi, dihin ʿūd
Hello. This is the best one I've got: oud oil.
وَعَلَيْكُمْ السَّلَامْ. هٰذَا أَحْسَنْ وَاحِدْ عِنْدِي، دِهِنْ عُودْ
B
ما شاء الله، ريحته حلوة. بكم؟
mā shāʼ allāh, rīḥtah ḥilwa. b-cham?
Wow, it smells lovely. How much?
مَا شَاءْ اللّٰهْ، رِيحْتَهْ حِلْوَة. بْكَمْ؟
A
بميتين. هو أغلى واحد هني. تبيه؟
b-mītēn. huwa aghla wāḥid hni. tabīh?
Two hundred. It's the most expensive one here. Do you want it?
بْمِيتَيْنْ. هُوَ أَغْلَى وَاحِدْ هْنِي. تَبِيهْ؟
B
غالي شوي. آخر سعر؟
ghāli shwayy. ākhir siʿir?
That's a bit expensive. What's your best price?
غَالِي شْوَيّْ. آخِرْ سِعِرْ؟
A
عشانك، بمية وخمسين. آخر كلام
ʿashānak, b-miya w khamsīn. ākhir kalām
For you, a hundred and fifty. That's my last word.
عَشَانَكْ، بْمِيَة وْخَمْسِينْ. آخِرْ كَلَامْ
B
خلاص، باخذه. هدية حلوة!
khalāṣ, bākhdhah. hadiyya ḥilwa!
OK, I'll take it. A lovely present!
خَلَاصْ، بَاخْذَهْ. هَدِيَّة حِلْوَة!
items: for a feminine thing: aḥsan waḥda
for you, for your sake (to a man)
culture: Bargaining is normal in the old souqs, such as the spice and perfume souqs in Deira, but not in malls and chain shops, where prices are fixed. Oud oil (dihin ʿūd) and bukhūr (incense) are classic Gulf presents.

title: Taking it back
goal: Return a watch that doesn't work to a shop assistant (a woman) and ask for one like your friend's
tip: mithil 'like' goes before a noun or takes an ending: mithil sāʿat rbīʿi 'like my friend's watch', mithilha 'like it (f.)'. Emiratis also say shrāt: shrāt-ha 'just like it'. ishtarēt 'I bought' ends like sawwēt.
grammar: mithil + noun or ending 'like' (mithil sāʿat rbīʿi, mithilha); UAE shrāt
dialogue: B
مساء الخير. اشتريت هالساعة أمس، بس ما تشتغل
masāʼ il-khēr. ishtarēt has-sāʿa ams, bas ma tishtaghil
Good evening. I bought this watch yesterday, but it doesn't work.
مَسَاءْ الْخَيْرْ. اِشْتَرَيْتْ هَالسَّاعَة أَمْسْ، بَسْ مَا تِشْتَغِلْ
A
مساء النور. خربانة؟ عندك الفاتورة؟
masāʼ in-nūr. kharbāna? ʿindak il-fātūra?
Good evening. Broken? Do you have the receipt?
مَسَاءْ النُّورْ. خَرْبَانَة؟ عِنْدَكْ الْفَاتُورَة؟
B
هيه، تفضلي. أبي أبدلها
hē, tfaẓẓali. abi abaddilha
Yes, here you are. I want to exchange it.
هَيْه، تْفَضَّلِي. أَبِي أَبَدِّلْهَا
A
أكيد. تبي وحدة ثانية شراتها؟
akīd. tabi waḥda thānya shrāt-ha?
Sure. Do you want another one just like it?
أَكِيدْ. تَبِي وَحْدَة ثَانْيَة شْرَاتْهَا؟
B
لا، أبي وحدة مثل ساعة ربيعي، أكبر شوي
la, abi waḥda mithil sāʿat rbīʿi, akbar shwayy
No, I want one like my friend's watch, a bit bigger.
لَا، أَبِي وَحْدَة مِثِلْ سَاعَةْ رْبِيعِي، أَكْبَرْ شْوَيّْ
A
هذيك؟ هي أغلى بخمسين درهم
hādhīch? hiya aghla b-khamsīn dirham
That one? It's fifty dirhams more.
هٰذِيكْ؟ هِيَ أَغْلَى بْخَمْسِينْ دِرْهَمْ
B
مب مشكلة، باخذها
mub mushkila, bākhidhha
No problem, I'll take it.
مُبْ مُشْكِلَة، بَاخِذْهَا
items: I bought; you bought (to a man)
to a woman: ishtarēti (اشتريتي); you'll also hear shirēt (شريت)
it doesn't work (a feminine thing: a watch, a car)
for a masculine thing: ma yishtaghil (ما يشتغل)
abi abaddilha = I want to exchange it; for a masculine thing: abaddlah (أبدله)
for a masculine thing: wāḥid thāni
the default is mithil (مثل); shrāt-ha = just like it (f.)

title: Splitting the bill
goal: Pay at a café with Sēf: insist on sharing and say how you will pay; Sēf leaves the change
tip: Recap: compare places with aḥsan min and arkhaṣ; mithil also makes 'as usual': mithil kill marra. Paying: adfaʿ 'I pay', badfaʿ 'I'll pay', tidfaʿ? 'are you paying?'. nuṣṣ nuṣṣ 'half and half' splits the bill between two.
dialogue: A
والله الأكل هني أحسن من المول، مثل كل مرة
wallāh il-akil hni aḥsan min il-mōl, mithil kill marra
Honestly, the food here is better than at the mall, as usual.
وَاللّٰهْ الْأَكِلْ هْنِي أَحْسَنْ مِنْ الْمَوْلْ، مِثِلْ كِلّْ مَرَّة
B
صح، وأرخص بعد. الحساب لو سمحت!
ṣaḥḥ, w arkhaṣ baʿad. il-ḥsāb law samaḥt!
True, and cheaper too. The bill, please!
صَحّْ، وْأَرْخَصْ بَعَدْ. الْحْسَابْ لَوْ سَمَحْتْ!
A
خلها علي اليوم
khallha ʿalay il-yōm
It's on me today.
خَلّْهَا عَلَيْ الْيَوْمْ
B
لا والله، كل مرة انت تدفع! نص نص
la wallāh, kill marra inta tidfaʿ! nuṣṣ nuṣṣ
No way, you pay every time! Let's go halves.
لَا وَاللّٰهْ، كِلّْ مَرَّة اِنْتَ تِدْفَعْ! نُصّْ نُصّْ
A
زين. تدفع كاش ولّا بطاقة؟
zēn. tidfaʿ kāsh walla biṭāga?
OK. Are you paying cash or card?
زَيْنْ. تِدْفَعْ كَاشْ وَلَّا بِطَاقَة؟
B
بطاقة، ما عندي فلوس في جيبي
biṭāga, ma ʿindi flūs fi jēbi
Card, I don't have any money on me.
بِطَاقَة، مَا عِنْدِي فْلُوسْ فِي جَيْبِي
A
عادي، أنا أدفع كاش، والباقي له
ʿādi, ana adfaʿ kāsh, w il-bāgi lah
No problem, I'm paying cash, and he can keep the change.
عَادِي، أَنَا أَدْفَعْ كَاشْ، وْالْبَاقِي لَهْ
items: half and half, let's go halves
culture: Friends often argue over the bill (la wallāh! ʿala ḥsābi!), and the one who invited usually pays. Young friends and colleagues also split it (nuṣṣ nuṣṣ). When an elder or a host has invited you, let them pay and thank them.

title: Checkpoint 2.2: a present for Sēf's mum
goal: Call Sēf, who is shopping with Fahad: ask the group what they're doing, compare presents and offer to chip in
tip: To a group, past verbs take -tu (ligētu 'you found') and present verbs -ūn (shu gāʿdīn tsawwūn?). shu raʼyak? becomes shu raʼykum? for a group; before a verb it means 'how about…?': shu raʼykum nrūḥ? aḥla shay 'the best thing' is a superlative.
grammar: checkpoint 2.2: recycle s2u018–s2u035 (gāʿid, comparatives, superlatives, mithil)
dialogue: B
ألو سيف، شو قاعدين تسوون؟
alō Sēf, shu gāʿdīn tsawwūn?
Hello Sēf, what are you guys doing?
أَلَوْ سَيْفْ، شُو قَاعْدِينْ تْسَوُّونْ؟
A
هلا! أنا وفهد في المول، نشتري هدية حق أمي
hala! ana w Fahad fi l-mōl, nishtiri hadiyya ḥagg ummi
Hi! Fahad and I are at the mall, buying a present for my mum.
هَلَا! أَنَا وْفَهَدْ فِي الْمَوْلْ، نِشْتِرِي هَدِيَّة حَقّْ أُمِّي
B
حلو! لقيتوا شي؟
ḥilu! ligētu shay?
Nice! Have you found anything?
حِلُو! لِقَيْتُوا شَيْ؟
A
لا، ما اشترينا شي. الساعات هني كلها مثل بعض
la, ma ishtarēna shay. is-sāʿāt hni killha mithil baʿaẓ
No, we haven't bought anything. The watches here are all the same.
لَا، مَا اِشْتَرَيْنَا شَيْ. السَّاعَاتْ هْنِي كِلّْهَا مِثِلْ بَعَضْ
B
شو رأيكم نروح سوق العطور في ديرة؟
shu raʼykum nrūḥ sūg il-ʿuṭūr fi Dēra?
How about we go to the perfume souq in Deira?
شُو رَأْيْكُمْ نْرُوحْ سُوقْ الْعُطُورْ فِي دَيْرَة؟
A
فكرة حلوة، بس ما عندي بيزات وايد
fikra ḥilwa, bas ma ʿindi bēzāt wāyid
Good idea, but I haven't got much money.
فِكْرَة حِلْوَة، بَسْ مَا عِنْدِي بَيْزَاتْ وَايِدْ
B
عادي، أنا بعد بدفع. والعطر أحلى شي!
ʿādi, ana baʿad badfaʿ. w il-ʿiṭir aḥla shay!
No problem, I'll pay too. And perfume's the best thing to get!
عَادِي، أَنَا بَعَدْ بَدْفَعْ. وْالْعِطِرْ أَحْلَى شَيْ!
items: to one man: ligēt; to one woman: ligēti; ligētu shay? = have you found anything?
ma ishtarēna shay = we haven't bought anything
what do you think? how about…? (to a group)
to one man: shu raʼyak? (شو رأيك); to one woman: shu raʼyich?; you'll also hear shrāykum? (شرايكم؟)
the best thing, the nicest thing

title: Grandad's old house
goal: Look at an old photo with Sēf and ask what his grandad's house was like
tip: Gulf has no 'is' in the present, but the past needs kān 'was': il-bēt kān ṣghīr. With a feminine subject it's kānat: kānat il-manṭiga hādya. kān fī 'there was' and ma kān fī 'there wasn't' never change. kān ʿindi 'I had' (with a feminine thing, also kānat ʿindi).
grammar: kān 'was': kān, kānat; kān fī 'there was'; kān ʿind- 'had'
dialogue: A
شوف، هذا بيت يدي أيام زمان
shūf, hādha bēt yaddi ayyām zamān
Look, this was my grandad's house in the old days.
شُوفْ، هٰذَا بَيْتْ يَدِّي أَيَّامْ زَمَانْ
B
ما شاء الله! كان أكبر من بيتكم؟
mā shāʼ allāh! kān akbar min bētkum?
Wow! Was it bigger than your house?
مَا شَاءْ اللّٰهْ! كَانْ أَكْبَرْ مِنْ بَيْتْكُمْ؟
A
لا، كان أصغر. بس كان في حوش كبير
la, kān aṣghar. bas kān fī ḥōsh kbīr
No, it was smaller. But there was a big courtyard.
لَا، كَانْ أَصْغَرْ. بَسْ كَانْ فِي حَوْشْ كْبِيرْ
B
وكان عندكم مكيف؟
w kān ʿindakum mkayyif?
And did your family have air conditioning?
وْكَانْ عِنْدَكُمْ مْكَيِّفْ؟
A
لا والله، ما كان في مكيف. والصيف كان صعب
la wallāh, ma kān fī mkayyif. w iṣ-ṣēf kān ṣaʿb
No, there was no air conditioning. And summer was hard.
لَا وَاللّٰهْ، مَا كَانْ فِي مْكَيِّفْ. وْالصَّيْفْ كَانْ صَعْبْ
B
والبيت الحين موجود؟
w il-bēt il-ḥīn mawjūd?
And is the house still there now?
وْالْبَيْتْ الْحِينْ مَوْجُودْ؟
A
لا، راح. كانت المنطقة هادية، الحين زحمة
la, rāḥ. kānat il-manṭiga hādya, il-ḥīn zaḥma
No, it's gone. The area was quiet; now it's packed.
لَا، رَاحْ. كَانَتْ الْمَنْطِقَة هَادْيَة، الْحِينْ زَحْمَة
items: kān doesn't change: kān fī ḥōsh
did you have? (to a group or a family)
to one man: kān ʿindak?; to one woman: kān ʿindich?; I had: kān ʿindi
the old days, back in the day

title: When I was little
goal: At Sēf's home, with Sēf there: greet Umm Sēf, ask after her and about her childhood, and tell her about yours
tip: kān + a present-tense verb means 'used to': kinna nilʿab 'we used to play', kint arūḥ 'I used to go'. Both verbs agree with the subject: kinti tsawwīn? 'did you use to do?' (to a woman). lamma kint ṣghīr 'when I was little' (a woman: ṣghīra).
grammar: kān + present verb = 'used to' (kint arūḥ, kinna nilʿab); lamma 'when'
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم يا أم سيف، شحالج؟
as-salāmu ʿalaykum yā Umm Sēf, shḥālich?
Hello, Umm Sēf, how are you?
السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ يَا أُمّْ سَيْفْ، شْحَالِجْ؟
A
وعليكم السلام، بخير الحمد لله. وأهلك؟ عساهم بخير؟
wa ʿalaykum is-salām, b-khēr il-ḥamdu lillāh. w ahlak? ʿasāhum b-khēr?
Hello, fine, thank God. And your family? I hope they're well?
وَعَلَيْكُمْ السَّلَامْ، بْخَيْرْ الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهْ. وْأَهْلَكْ؟ عَسَاهُمْ بْخَيْرْ؟
B
الحمد لله بخير. سيف يقول كنتي ساكنة في ديرة؟
il-ḥamdu lillāh b-khēr. Sēf ygūl kinti sākna fi Dēra?
They're fine, thank God. Sēf says you used to live in Deira?
الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰهْ بْخَيْرْ. سَيْفْ يْقُولْ كِنْتِي سَاكْنَة فِي دَيْرَة؟
A
هيه، أيام زمان كنا ساكنين في ديرة، قريب من البحر
hē, ayyām zamān kinna sāknīn fi Dēra, garīb min il-baḥar
Yes, in the old days we lived in Deira, near the sea.
هَيْه، أَيَّامْ زَمَانْ كِنَّا سَاكْنِينْ فِي دَيْرَة، قَرِيبْ مِنْ الْبَحَرْ
B
وشو كنتي تسوين كل يوم؟
w shu kinti tsawwīn kill yōm?
And what did you use to do every day?
وْشُو كِنْتِي تْسَوِّينْ كِلّْ يَوْمْ؟
A
كنا نلعب في الفريج ويا العيال، أحلى شي!
kinna nilʿab fi l-firīj wiyya l-ʿyāl, aḥla shay!
We used to play in the neighbourhood with the other kids, the best thing ever!
كِنَّا نِلْعَبْ فِي الْفِرِيجْ وِيَّا الْعْيَالْ، أَحْلَى شَيْ!
B
أنا لما كنت صغير، كنت أروح المدرسة وأرجع البيت، بس!
ana lamma kint ṣghīr, kint arūḥ il-madrasa w arjaʿ il-bēt, bas!
When I was little, I just went to school and came home!
أَنَا لَمَّا كِنْتْ صْغِيرْ، كِنْتْ أَرُوحْ الْمَدْرَسَة وْأَرْجَعْ الْبَيْتْ، بَسْ!
items: when I was little (said by a man)
a woman says: lamma kint ṣghīra; more often: yōm kint ṣghīr (yōm + past is taught in s2u044)
I was; you were (to a man)
to a woman: kinti; kint + verb = I used to: kint arūḥ
the neighbourhood (old-style, where families know each other)
culture: Before oil was found in 1966 (first shipped in 1969), many Dubai families lived from the sea: pearling, fishing and trade along the Creek, with Deira on one bank and Bur Dubai on the other. Life centred on the firīj, the neighbourhood where everyone knew each other; the Emirati cartoon Freej (2006) is named after it.

title: Dubai used to be different
goal: At the office, talk with Maryam about how Dubai has changed since she was a child
tip: kān works with comparatives too: kānat iz-zaḥma aqall 'the traffic was lighter', awwal kān ahda 'it used to be quieter' (awwal = before, in the old days). For 'used to', kān agrees with the subject: kintu trūḥūn 'you (all) used to go', kānaw yaʿarfūn 'they used to know'.
grammar: kān + present verb for groups (kintu trūḥūn, kānaw yaʿarfūn); kān + comparative
dialogue: A
تدري؟ لما كنت صغيرة، ما كان في مترو
tadri? lamma kint ṣghīra, ma kān fī mitrō
You know what? When I was little, there was no metro.
تَدْرِي؟ لَمَّا كِنْتْ صْغِيرَة، مَا كَانْ فِي مِتْرَوْ
B
والله؟ يعني كنتوا تروحون كل مكان بالسيارة؟
wallāh? yaʿni kintu trūḥūn kill makān bis-sayyāra?
Really? So you all used to go everywhere by car?
وَاللّٰهْ؟ يَعْنِي كِنْتُوا تْرُوحُونْ كِلّْ مَكَانْ بِالسَّيَّارَة؟
A
هيه، بس الزحمة كانت أقل من الحين
hē, bas iz-zaḥma kānat aqall min il-ḥīn
Yes, but there was less traffic than now.
هَيْه، بَسْ الزَّحْمَة كَانَتْ أَقَلّْ مِنْ الْحِينْ
B
والحين دبي أكبر بوايد
w il-ḥīn Dbayy akbar b-wāyid
And now Dubai's much bigger.
وْالْحِينْ دْبَيّْ أَكْبَرْ بْوَايِدْ
A
أكيد! والناس كانوا يعرفون بعض
akīd! w in-nās kānaw yaʿarfūn baʿaẓ
Of course! And people used to know each other.
أَكِيدْ! وْالنَّاسْ كَانَوْا يَعَرْفُونْ بَعَضْ
B
دبي تغيرت وايد. أول كان أحسن؟
Dbayy tghayyarat wāyid. awwal kān aḥsan?
Dubai has changed a lot. Was it better before?
دْبَيّْ تْغَيَّرَتْ وَايِدْ. أَوَّلْ كَانْ أَحْسَنْ؟
A
ما أدري. الحين أحسن، بس أول كان أهدى
ma adri. il-ḥīn aḥsan, bas awwal kān ahda
I don't know. It's better now, but it used to be quieter.
مَا أَدْرِي. الْحِينْ أَحْسَنْ، بَسْ أَوَّلْ كَانْ أَهْدَى
items: to one man: kint; to one woman: kinti; kintu trūḥūn = you used to go (to a group)
I've changed (become different): tghayyart; 'I changed something' is ghayyart (غيرت)

title: How long have you been here?
goal: Answer a new Emirati colleague: how long you've been in Dubai and learning Arabic, and whether you're used to it
tip: ṣār-li + a time says how long something has gone on: ṣār-li sana fi Dbayy 'I've been in Dubai a year'. Add a verb for 'have been doing': ṣār-li sitt shhūr atʿallam. Ask with cham: cham ṣār-lak? (to a woman: ṣār-lich).
grammar: ṣār-li + time 'I've been … for': ṣār-li sana; cham ṣār-lak?
dialogue: A
انت من بريطانيا؟ كم صار لك في دبي؟
inta min Brīṭānya? cham ṣār-lak fi Dbayy?
Are you from Britain? How long have you been in Dubai?
اِنْتَ مِنْ بْرِيطَانْيَا؟ كَمْ صَارْ لَكْ فِي دْبَيّْ؟
B
صار لي سنة تقريبا. أول كنت في لندن
ṣār-li sana tagrīban. awwal kint fi Landan
About a year. Before that I was in London.
صَارْ لِي سَنَة تَقْرِيبًا. أَوَّلْ كِنْتْ فِي لَنْدَنْ
A
ما شاء الله، وتتكلم عربي زين!
mā shāʼ allāh, w titkallam ʿarabi zēn!
Great, and you speak Arabic well!
مَا شَاءْ اللّٰهْ، وْتِتْكَلَّمْ عَرَبِي زَيْنْ!
B
شوي شوي. صار لي ست شهور أتعلم
shwayy shwayy. ṣār-li sitt shhūr atʿallam
Little by little. I've been learning for six months.
شْوَيّْ شْوَيّْ. صَارْ لِي سِتّْ شْهُورْ أَتْعَلَّمْ
A
وتعودت على دبي؟
w tʿawwadt ʿala Dbayy?
And have you got used to Dubai?
وْتْعَوَّدْتْ عَلَى دْبَيّْ؟
B
هيه، بس الحر صعب علي. البرد أحسن!
hē, bas il-ḥarr ṣaʿb ʿalay. il-bard aḥsan!
Yes, but the heat's hard for me. The cold is better!
هَيْه، بَسْ الْحَرّْ صَعْبْ عَلَيْ. الْبَرْدْ أَحْسَنْ!
A
عادي، بعد سنتين بتتعود!
ʿādi, baʿd santēn bititʿawwad!
That's normal, give it two years and you'll get used to it!
عَادِي، بَعْدْ سَنْتَيْنْ بِتِتْعَوَّدْ!
items: ṣār-lah = he's been; ṣār-lha = she's been
how long have you been (here)? (to a man)
to a woman: cham ṣār-lich? (كم صار لج)
I've got used to; you've got used to (to a man)
you'll get used to it (to a man)
